content.title: About
content.content: Seedless watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a fruit from which the seeds have been removed; this entry offers only the raw rind. The rind is rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals but has a tougher texture and a slightly bitter taste compared with the flesh.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Watermelon rind contains over 10 % dietary fiber, making it an excellent source of roughage.
The rind is a good source of lycopene, the same antioxidant found in the red flesh.
Seedless varieties were developed by breeders in the early 20th century for easier consumption.
In some traditional cuisines the rind is used to make pickles and marinades.
Raw rind retains most B‑vitamins, which can degrade with heat.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The rind provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene acts as a powerful antioxidant, supporting heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Raw rind supplies vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Potassium, magnesium, and small amounts of calcium are present, helping maintain electrolyte balance.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Approximately 30 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Hard-to-digest fiber
items.content: Large amounts of fiber may cause bloating or discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Bitter flavor
items.content: The rind’s natural bitterness can be off‑putting without proper preparation.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If not organically grown, residues may remain on the skin; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the rind thinly and add it to salads, smoothies, or pickle it. To soften the flavor, blanch the rind in boiling water for 1–2 minutes, then shock in ice water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the rind in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze it in bags for up to 3 months.
